module MyGem
  # Deprecator instance owned by the gem (Rails 7.1+ style; the class-level
  # ActiveSupport::Deprecation.warn call is no longer available on current Rails).
  @deprecator = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("2.0", "MyGem")

  class << self
    attr_reader :deprecator

    def old_api
      deprecator.warn("old_api is deprecated")
      42
    end
  end
end

module ReportFormatter
  # Formats a time using Rails' built-in :db format, e.g. "2026-01-02 03:04:05".
  def self.stamp(time)
    time.to_fs(:db)
  end

  # Formats a date using Rails' built-in :long format, e.g. "January 02, 2026".
  def self.long_date(date)
    date.to_fs(:long)
  end
end

module ReportFormatter
  # Requires ActiveSupport (Rails) to be loaded; do not add require calls here.
  # Uses Rails' built-in named formats: Time::DATE_FORMATS[:db] and Date::DATE_FORMATS[:long].
  # Rails 7.1+ uses to_fs for named formats (to_s(format) was removed).

  def self.stamp(time)
    time.to_fs(:db)
  end

  def self.long_date(date)
    date.to_fs(:long)
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  def create
    user_params = params.require(:user)

    # A plain string (or array) in place of the nested user object is a
    # malformed request; params.permit would raise NoMethodError on it.
    unless user_params.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
      return render json: { error: "user must be a nested object" }, status: :bad_request
    end

    # Only :name is permitted; any other keys are silently dropped.
    permitted = user_params.permit(:name)

    render json: permitted.to_h, status: :ok
  rescue ActionController::ParameterMissing
    render json: { error: "user parameter is required" }, status: :bad_request
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  def create
    render json: user_params, status: :ok
  end

  private

  # params.expect (Rails 8.0+) validates the shape of user[...]. When user is a
  # plain string, it raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, which Rails maps
  # to HTTP 400. Keys other than name are dropped.
  def user_params
    params.expect(user: [:name])
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :render_bad_request

  def create
    # A plain string (or array) in place of the nested user object is a client error.
    unless params[:user].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
      return render_bad_request(message: "param 'user' must be a nested object")
    end

    # permit drops every key that is not explicitly allowed.
    user_params = params.require(:user).permit(:name)

    render json: user_params.to_h, status: :ok
  end

  private

  def render_bad_request(exception = nil, message: nil)
    message ||= exception&.message || "bad request"
    render json: { error: message }, status: :bad_request
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  def create
    user = params.require(:user)

    # `user` must be a nested object (user[name]=...), not a plain string or array.
    unless user.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
      return render_bad_request
    end

    # Only :name is permitted; any other keys are silently dropped.
    render json: user.permit(:name).to_h, status: :ok
  rescue ActionController::ParameterMissing
    render_bad_request
  end

  private

  def render_bad_request
    render json: { error: "user must be a nested object with permitted parameters" },
           status: :bad_request
  end
end
